title: Inside the Story
objectives: I can use ten story words to talk about what I read.
I can tell the difference between a myth and a legend.
I can tell about the plot, the villain, and the hero in a story.
I can retell a story using words from this unit.
rationale: Third graders retell stories and talk about how they work, so they need the words readers use: dialogue, plot, and episode name parts of a story; myth and legend name kinds of old stories; villain, quest, courage, and heroic name what happens and who does it; mysterious describes the tone. Three are Tier 3 literary terms (dialogue, plot, myth); the rest are the Tier 2 words that fill retellings. The passage models how to use them in a conversation about a story, and the produce tasks ask students to retell a story they know with at least four of the words.

passage.title: Story Time at Lantern Hill
paras: At Lantern Hill School, Friday was story time. This week, Ms. Park read an old myth that explained why stars twinkle. It told about a girl named Nina, who went on a quest to bring back a missing star.

The plot was simple. A villain named Mr. Gloom had stolen the star, and the whole village went dark. Nina was small, but she had great courage. "I will bring it back," she said. The class loved the dialogue, because Nina's words were short and bold.

Each part of the tale was like a short episode. In one, a mysterious owl asked Nina three riddles. In another, she crossed a bridge of fog. At the end, Nina won the star back and hung it in the sky, and the village glowed again.

Afterward, Ms. Park told a legend from their own town about a heroic fisherman who rescued a boat in a storm. "Some stories are made up," she said, "and some begin with real people. Both can teach us something."

qs.why: Nina goes to bring back a missing star, so a quest is a long search to find something.

qs.q: Why did the whole village go dark?
choices: The owl blew out the lights.

qs.q: Which detail best shows that Nina has courage?
choices: She hung the star in the sky.
She asked an owl for riddles.
She said, "I will bring it back," and went on the quest.
qs.why: Courage means facing a hard task even if you are afraid; Nina speaks boldly and goes.

qs.q: What is a central idea of the passage?
choices: Old stories can explain the world and teach us lessons.
Teachers should read only on Fridays.
qs.why: Ms. Park reads a myth and tells a legend, and says that both can teach us something.

teacher.overview: Students learn ten literary words, read a short story in which a teacher shares a myth and a legend, and use the words to retell a story and discuss its parts.

notes.va.dialogue.n: Dialogue is what characters say. Show quotation marks in a page and ask who is speaking.
notes.va.plot.n: Plot is what happens in order. Use the beginning, middle, and end boxes. Do not confuse with a garden plot.
notes.va.myth.n: Myth explains nature or beginnings. Ask: what does this story explain? Contrast with legend.
notes.va.villain.n: A villain works against the hero. Students may think a villain must be scary; a sneaky or selfish character counts too.
notes.va.legend.n: A legend is an old hero story, often tied to a real person or place. Compare with a myth: myths explain nature; legends celebrate heroes.
notes.va.quest.n: A quest is a long search with an important goal. Ask what the goal is and what gets in the way.
notes.va.mysterious.adj: Mysterious is strange and unexplained. Show a clue-in-a-box activity and have students describe it. Link to mystery.
notes.va.courage.n: Courage is acting while afraid. Students may think brave people are never scared; stress that fear and courage can go together.
notes.va.episode.n: An episode is one part of a longer story or show. Use a favorite series as an example.
notes.va.heroic.adj: Heroic means brave and helpful to others. Compare with brave: heroic usually involves helping someone else.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: "The story says Mr. Gloom stole the star. He causes the problem, so he is the villain. Nina goes on a long search to bring it back, so that is a quest. I can tell the plot by saying the problem and how it was solved."
